subject: Reserved commit term and staggered start options for OrbiData Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbiData Procurement <procurement@orbidata.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved commit term and start scheduling

Hi Chloe —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the workload estimates with our infra team and want to discuss reserved commits for Dedicated (GPU pools) and how Redwood handles phased onramp across regions. High-level asks:

- Pricing tiers and discounts for 12/24/36 month reserved commits
- Options to phase capacity start across US-East and US-West (we'd like a two-stage start over ~6 weeks)
- Throughput guarantees (QPS/token/sec) and how they map to GPU pool sizes
- Any credit/price protection if we bump up commit after month 3

I've attached our capacity spreadsheet (OrbiData_Capacity_Requirements.xlsx). Can you propose a few packaging options and an indicative timeline? Procurement (cc'ed) will need an invoice cadence and PO-language for any deferred starts.

Best,
Daniel
Director of Infrastructure
OrbiData

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term and start scheduling

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Attached is a short pricing summary (Dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) and one-page phasing example. High-level options we recommend based on your load profile: 

1) 12-month (flex) — 8% base discount, immediate start window within 30 days, limited credit on upsizes (not recommended if you want price protection).
2) 24-month (standard) — 12% base discount, supports a staged onboard (we can stagger capacity over up to 8 weeks), 6% credit on upsizes in first 90 days.
3) 36-month (commit) — 18% base discount, includes price protection for incremental adds in first 180 days, priority capacity reservations and better SLA terms.

Phasing example (for your two-stage US start):
- Stage 1 (US-East) active at T+30 days: 60% of committed capacity (target latency SLO 95th pct < 120ms).
- Stage 2 (US-West) active at T+75 days: remaining 40% capacity.

Throughput mapping (ballpark): 1x A100-80GB-equivalent GPU (shared pool instance) ~ supports ~120 - 180 steady QPS for typical chat workloads at 2k token windows with our batching. We'll have Rishi follow up with precise sizing tied to the workbook.

Two quick asks from our side before we give a formal quote:
- Confirm final expected peak QPS and token distribution (attached workbook helps; a single-sheet with peak-per-region is ideal).
- Confirm preferred invoice cadence (annual, quarterly, monthly).

If that works I can loop in our contracts specialist and share a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Thanks —
Chloe
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbiData Procurement <procurement@orbidata.com>, Maya Li <maya.li@orbidata.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term and start scheduling

Chloe —

Thanks for the options. A few clarifications: 

- We plan a two-region rollout but would like the ability to shift the stage 2 start earlier if we see run-rate growth. Any constraints?
- Can you confirm the SLOs & credits if you miss throughput targets? We need something procurement-safe.
- As for cadence, procurement prefers quarterly invoicing but will accept annual prepay for a larger credit.

Procurement attached a draft SOW and PO template. Also, to be explicit: we're evaluating 24 vs 36 months, but the procurement team may push back on long prepayments.

Let me know if your team can do a draft term sheet reflecting a 24-month recommendation with a phaseable start and conditional credit for missed SLOs.

—Daniel

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term and start scheduling

Daniel / Chloe —

I dug into the workbook and sketched a sizing model (attached: throughput_sizing_calc.csv). Notes: 

- For the workload shape you shared (peak 2.5k QPS combined, 70% traffic to US-East), a safe starting commit is 18 A100-eq GPUs spread in a pool (12 in US-East, 6 in US-West staged). That maps to ~2,160 steady QPS with headroom for bursty traffic via autoscaling/burst buckets.
- Latency SLOs: we can commit to 95th pct < 140ms for the committed pool under normal load; a credit ladder applies if we miss (1% service credit per 24 hrs of qualifying degradation, capped at 10% monthly). We will document the exact measurement windows and failure modes in the term sheet.
- If you plan to shift stage 2 earlier, we support a single-step stage-advance call if capacity is available; otherwise we will ramp as capacity allows. For guaranteed early-stage activation we recommend a narrow start gate (e.g., earliest T+28 days with a short notice window) and a small buffer credit if we can't meet the new date due to capacity constraints.

Operational suggestion: reserve + burst model — commit baseline pool for steady-state plus a small burst reserve for peak spikes. That materially reduces your unit cost but preserves tail latency.

Happy to walk through the calc on a short call.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbiData Procurement <procurement@orbidata.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T11:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term and start scheduling — commercial proposal

Hi Daniel —

Following Rishi's sizing, finance reviewed options and we can propose a commercial structure that balances procurement preferences and your desire for price protection: 

- 24-month option (recommended): 12% discount off list; quarterly invoicing by default; option to prepay annually for an additional 3% credit. Upsize credit: 6% credit applied to the next invoice if you increase committed GPU count within first 90 days. Deferred-start: we can defer billing for up to 90 days from signature with a small 1.5% deferred-start fee on the first invoice.
- 36-month option: 16% discount; annual prepay receives 5% extra credit; upsizes within 180 days protected at the original discount.

We can include a SLAs appendix with the credit ladder Rishi mentioned and explicit measurement definitions. For PO language, procurement's template looked fine; we'll add a clause on phased activation dates and a rollback/advance process.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Chloe to share a 24-month term sheet with the phasing schedule and DocuSign link.
2) OrbiData to confirm invoice cadence (quarterly vs annual prepay) and sign the SOW/PO.

I can draft an amendment for the deferred-start clause if you'd like the flexibility.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orbidata.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbiData Procurement <procurement@orbidata.com>, Maya Li <maya.li@orbidata.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit term and start scheduling — commercial proposal

Neha / Chloe —

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. OrbiData is willing to move forward on the 24-month option with quarterly invoicing and the 90-day deferred-start window. We request the 6% upsizing credit to explicitly apply to any mid-term increases within the first 120 days instead of 90; procurement says that gives them the runway to validate sustained usage.

If you can update the term sheet to reflect 24-month / quarterly invoicing / upsizing credit window to 120 days, we'll route the PO this week. Attached is a signed PO placeholder (OrbiData_PO_08020.pdf) — we'll finalize once the DocuSign term sheet lands.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

—Daniel
Director of Infrastructure, OrbiData
